//: OPTIONAL CONVENIENCE. Railway deploys this service without this file — it detects package.json and runs the build and start scripts. The file exists so the health check and the restart policy are recorded in the repository rather than clicked into a dashboard nobody can diff. Nothing in the service reads it, and its absence changes no behaviour.

build.//: DOCKERFILE rather than NIXPACKS so the image is byte-identical to what Fly and Render build, and to what a developer builds locally. One build definition, three hosts.

deploy.//: The start command is the Dockerfile's CMD. Not repeated here: two places to change it is one place to forget.
deploy.//restart: ON_FAILURE with a bounded retry. ALWAYS would mask a configuration error as a restart loop — src/config.ts exits 1 on a missing REALTIME_SHARED_SECRET, and that must surface as a failed deploy, not as a service that flaps forever while students see a dead chat.
deploy.//replicas: ONE. The rate limiter and the presence registry are per-process Maps (see src/ratelimit.ts): with two replicas behind a load balancer, a user's two tabs can land on different instances and get double budget, and presence counts split. Scaling out requires a shared store, which this stack does not have.
